greta is one package, but it is also a small family of them.

The core package gives you the modelling language. The extension packages add
particular kinds of model on top of it, and they all work with the same greta
arrays, the same `model()`, and the same `mcmc()`.

### greta

The core package. Write a statistical model in R code, then fit it with MCMC.

```r
install.packages("greta")
```

[Go to docs...](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta/)

## Extension packages

These are not loaded with `library(greta)`, so you will need to load each one
with its own call to `library()`.

### greta.gp

Gaussian processes. Create and combine kernels, then use them to define either
full rank or sparse Gaussian processes.

```r
install.packages("greta.gp")
```

[Go to docs...](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/)

### greta.gam

Generalised additive models. Use mgcv's smoother functions and formula syntax
to define smooth terms, then write your own likelihood around them.

Returning to CRAN. In the meantime, install it from GitHub.

```r
pak::pak("greta-dev/greta.gam")
```

[Go to docs...](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gam/)

### greta.dynamics

Dynamical systems. Analyse transition matrices by iterating them to a stable
state, and solve ordinary differential equations.

```r
install.packages("greta.dynamics")
```

[Go to docs...](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.dynamics/)

### greta.distributions

Extra probability distributions that are not shipped with greta itself. Zero
inflated Poisson and negative binomial, discrete normal and lognormal,
conditional Bernoulli, and ordered logit.

On its way to CRAN. In the meantime, install it from GitHub.

```r
pak::pak("greta-dev/greta.distributions")
```

[Go to docs...](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.distributions/)

## Writing your own extension

If you want to build a package on top of greta, the internals are documented,
and the extension packages above are all reasonable things to read for a worked
example.

Have a look at [`?greta::internals`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta/reference/internals.html),
and at the [contribute](contribute.html) page.
